summary: Full backend + frontend E2E testing of AquaRekap (AMDK sales recap). Backend: 36 pytest cases across auth (cookies/bcrypt/refresh/logout), products, customers, transactions+filters, dashboard, rekap bulanan, export excel/pdf, CORS -> 34 passed / 2 failed (94.4%). Frontend: login (success + wrong password error), dashboard KPIs & charts, full transaction entry flow (customer -> default price type -> product -> variant -> auto price -> price-type change updates price -> manual price -> qty -> subtotal/total), save, status toggle, delete with confirm, all 3 filters (date range/customer/status), Excel+PDF downloads, Produk CRUD, Customer CRUD, Rekap Bulanan month switch, logout + protected-route guard. All frontend flows passed. All test data created was deleted (DB back to 3 products / 3 customers / 4 seed transactions).

critical.issue: No brute-force lockout / rate limiting. 6+ consecutive wrong-password attempts all return 401; playbook requires lockout (429) after 5 failed attempts.

minor.issue: Returns 200 'dihapus' for non-existent IDs (delete_one result not checked) instead of 404.
If the JWT sub no longer exists, `user` is None and `user['_id']` raises TypeError -> 500 instead of 401.
month/year are not range-validated; month=13 returns 200 with empty payload instead of 422.

issues: Uses native browser <input type="date"> pickers (mm/dd/yyyy locale format) instead of the shadcn Calendar/Popover component; inconsistent with the rest of the shadcn UI and shows US date format in an Indonesian app
Large empty whitespace below the card grid (only 3 cards); consider a min-height/empty-state layout

action_items: Add login brute-force lockout / rate limiting (429 after 5 failed attempts) per auth playbook
Return 404 on DELETE of non-existent product/customer/transaction (check delete_one deleted_count)
Guard /api/auth/refresh against missing user (return 401 instead of 500)
Optional: replace native date inputs with shadcn Calendar + Indonesian date formatting
critical_code_review_comments: server.py delete handlers ignore delete_one().deleted_count -> silently report success for unknown IDs
refresh_token(): `user = await db.users.find_one(...)` result is dereferenced without a None check
No rate limiting on /api/auth/login; single-admin app is exposed to credential brute force
Cookies use secure=True + samesite=none which is correct for the HTTPS preview, but will break plain-HTTP local dev; consider deriving from an env flag

Verified good: bcrypt hashes are $2b$, httpOnly cookies set, MongoDB _id excluded from all responses ({"_id": 0} projections), CORS echoes explicit origin with allow_credentials=true (preview ingress additionally rewrites ACAO to '*' - infra-level, not app), seed_admin re-hashes password when ADMIN_PASSWORD changes
seed_data_creation: Created and then deleted: TEST_PRODUK/TEST_PRODUK_EDIT, TEST_CUST/TEST_CUST_EDIT, TEST_PRODUK_UI2, TEST_CUST_UI2 and several TEST_ transactions (2026-07-05/10/15). DB verified back to original seed state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite lives at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope; TestDashboard consistency test has a 1x retry because parallel workers mutate transactions - run with -n 0 if you see cross-class flakiness). Known open failures: TestAuth::test_brute_force_lockout (no rate limiting) and TestProducts::test_delete_missing_product (200 instead of 404) - these are real app gaps, not test bugs. Frontend flows all verified once; re-verify only areas touched by fixes. Note /app/auth_testing.md does not exist in this workspace.
rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force failure: /api/auth/login has no attempt counter/lockout store, so every wrong password just raises 401. Delete-404 failure: handlers call db.<coll>.delete_one() and unconditionally return a success message without inspecting deleted_count.
